extracted.intended_audience: USPTO personnel, patent examiners, patent owners, patent practitioners, and third-party submitters
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements for submitting prior art or patent-owner written statements to patent files and for requesting and processing ex parte reexamination proceedings at the USPTO. Covers who may submit, what may be submitted, timing, required content, processing, and related certificate/closure rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may cite prior art or written statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person at any time may cite prior art patents or printed publications or patent-owner written statements to the Office (35 U.S.C. 301). 'Any person' includes corporate or governmental entities, patentees, licensees, reexamination requesters, real parties in interest, persons without a real interest, and persons acting for real parties in interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A third-party submitter may remain anonymous (identity excluded from the file) if confidentiality requested; reexamination requesters generally cannot remain anonymous due to certification requirements unless using a registered practitioner. Patent examiners must not create such submissions on their own initiative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted content of 35 U.S.C. 301 / 37 CFR 1.501 submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions are limited to: prior art consisting of patents or printed publications, and/or statements of the patent owner filed in a proceeding before a Federal court or the Office in which the patent owner took a position on the scope of any claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions must be directed only to patents, printed publications, and/or patent owner written claim scope statements and additional information. Submissions containing issues not so directed (e.g., 35 U.S.C. 112 objections, public use allegations, or commentary on patent owner conduct) should not be entered and should be returned, discarded, or closed (see MPEP §2206).

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation of pertinence and manner of applying prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: A submission must include an explanation in writing of the pertinence and manner of applying any prior art or written statement to at least one claim of the patent (37 CFR 1.501(b)(1) / 35 U.S.C. 301(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The explanation should, for at least one claim, set forth how each item cited shows or teaches at least one limitation of the claim (examples provided in MPEP). If filed by the patent owner, the submission may include an explanation of how the claims differ from the submitted prior art or written statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific identification requirements for written-statement submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions of patent-owner written statements (37 CFR 1.501(a)(2)/(a)(3)) must identify: (i) the forum and proceeding where the statement was filed; (ii) the specific papers and portions containing the statements; and (iii) how each statement is one in which the patent owner took a position on the scope of any claim of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identification of portions may be satisfied by citing documents and specific pages. The requirement prevents submission of mere restatements by other parties; submitters should include information about the status and relationship of the proceeding to the patent. Accompanying documents from the proceeding that address the written statement must be included (35 U.S.C. 301(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies and necessary English translations required
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of all submitted prior art patents, printed publications, or section 301 written statements and any necessary English translation must be included with the submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The copies and translations ensure that the information's value may be readily determined by persons inspecting the patent files and by an examiner during subsequent proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of service requirement for third-party submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: A submission by a person other than the patent owner must include a certification that a copy of the submission was served in its entirety upon the patent owner at the address provided in 37 CFR 1.33(c); failure to include proper proof of service will result in the submission not being entered (37 CFR 1.501(e)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If proper proof of service is missing, the submission will not be entered into the patent file. Confidential submissions should nevertheless include proper proof of service (submitted anonymously) or they will not be entered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redaction for protective orders and confidentiality handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Written statements and accompanying information that are subject to an applicable protective order must be submitted in redacted form to exclude information subject to that order (35 U.S.C. 301(d); 37 CFR 1.501(a)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon written request the identity of the person citing prior art/written statements shall be excluded from the patent file and kept confidential; anonymous submissions must be submitted without identification and with proper proof of service to be entered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing: when submissions may be filed (period of enforceability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions may be filed 'at any time' under 35 U.S.C. 301; rule-defined as 'any time during the period of enforceability of a patent' (generally term of the patent plus 6 years under 35 U.S.C. 286). If litigation is instituted within that period, submissions may be filed after statute expiration provided the patent is still enforceable against someone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions filed after the date of any order to reexamine will not be entered into the patent file until the pending reexamination is concluded (37 CFR 1.501(c)), except in limited exceptions (by patent owner; by an ex parte requester who files the fee and required documents; as an ex parte reply under 1.535; or as an enterable submission under 1.948 in inter partes reexamination). This rule helps prevent harassment via frequent submissions during reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry rules during pending reexamination (37 CFR 1.502 and 1.902)
rubrics_metrics.description: Citations by the patent owner and by an ex parte reexamination requester will be entered in the reexamination file during a reexamination proceeding. Entry in the patent file of citations submitted after an order to reexamine by persons other than the patent owner or the requester will be delayed until the reexamination proceeding has been terminated (37 CFR 1.502). Similar rules apply for inter partes reexamination (37 CFR 1.902).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This preserves orderly handling of documents and prevents third-party filings from affecting ongoing reexaminations until conclusion. See also rules for processing during merged/merged-with-inter-partes situations (MPEP references).

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility of Technology Center (TC) for processing submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions received will be forwarded to the Technology Center that currently examines the class and subclass of the patent; the TC must promptly determine whether the submission meets statutory and rule requirements and enter it into the patent file at the appropriate time if proper (MPEP §2206).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a submission is proper and filed prior to an order in any pending reexamination, it should be immediately entered. If filed after an order, it will be stored until conclusion and the patent owner and third-party submitter should be notified accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: What constitutes a 'proper' submission for entry
rubrics_metrics.description: A proper 37 CFR 1.501 submission is limited to patents, printed publications, and/or patent owner written claim scope statements and additional information and includes the requisite citation description (explanation of pertinence and manner of application) and proof of service (if by a third party).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any of these elements are missing (improper content, missing explanation, missing proof of service), the submission will not be entered and will be handled as described (returned, discarded, or closed), with notification to submitter/patent owner in many cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of improper submissions and notification procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: If a submission does not qualify for entry (not limited to permitted content or missing required information/proof of service), the third-party submitter (if known) and the patent owner may be notified that the citation submission is improper and is not being entered. The submission may be returned, discarded, or closed (MPEP §2206).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific handling depends on whether service was included and whether the identity of the submitter is known. If service was included and identity known, return/discard/close and notify submitter and patent owner; if service missing but identity known, return or notify; if identity unknown and no service, the submission may be discarded with limited notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on inclusion of non-patent-reference issues
rubrics_metrics.description: A submission cannot include any issue not directed to patents, printed publications, or patent owner written claim scope statements and additional information. For example, statements about violations of 35 U.S.C. 112, public use, or the conduct of the patent owner are not permitted and submissions containing such issues should not be entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions also should not include argument/discussion of references previously treated in the prosecution of the patent or in prior reexamination proceedings; if such extraneous issues are present, the submission should be returned/discarded/closed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavits or declarations may accompany submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits, declarations, or other written evidence relating to submitted documents may accompany a 37 CFR 1.501 submission to explain contents or pertinent dates; commercial-success affidavits or enablement evidence may be acceptable where relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These supporting documents can clarify dates, explain pertinence, or supply evidence of nonobviousness or lack of enablement tied to the cited documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: No filing fee required for 37 CFR 1.501 submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: A submission under 37 CFR 1.501 is not subject to a fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies to prior-art and written-statement submissions distinct from requests for reexamination which have separate fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential/anonymous submission handling and service obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: If a submitter wishes their identity excluded from the file and kept confidential, the submission papers must be submitted anonymously without any identification of the person making the submission; confidential submissions should include proper proof of service as required by 37 CFR 1.248(b) or they will not be entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For reexamination requests, a real party in interest may remain anonymous only by using a registered practitioner to file; the registered practitioner certifies compliance (including estoppel considerations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiners must not initiate or place submissions in patent files
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent examiners should not, at their own initiative, create a submission under 35 U.S.C. 301 and place it in a patent file or forward it for placement in the patent file; such activity is inappropriate because examiners are delegated responsibility for making patentability decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners performing such acts may inappropriately signal that claims are not patentable in matters outside those pending before them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry policy for patent-owner submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: If a proper 37 CFR 1.501 submission is filed by the patent owner, it should be entered in the file whether filed prior to or after an order for reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No notification to the patent owner is necessary when the patent owner files the submission; patent-owner submissions may include an explanation of how the claims differ from submitted prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification and storage when submission filed after reexamination order
rubrics_metrics.description: If a proper third-party submission is filed after an order for reexamination, it will be stored (closed) until the reexamination is concluded and not entered into the patent file at that time; the patent owner and third-party submitter (if known) should be notified of this action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the submission included service on the patent owner, the duplicate remains closed but is not entered until conclusion; notification enables patent owner to consider submitting the prior art under applicable reexamination owner-submission rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination certificate format, numbering, and content
rubrics_metrics.description: The ex parte reexamination certificate number is the patent number followed by a two-character kind-code suffix (first letter B for pre-2001, C for on/after Jan 2, 2001; second letter identifies number of reexamination). Certificates identify which claims are confirmed, canceled, disclaimed, or not examined, and print amended/new claims (new claims in italics; amended claims with italics and bracketing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certificates also list bibliographic information, representative claim text, any changes to specification/drawings, prior court decisions, and, if ordered under 35 U.S.C. 257, indicate that reexamination was ordered under that section. See MPEP §2290-§2293 for further formatting rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervening rights effect of amended/new claims after reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposed amended or new claim determined to be patentable and incorporated into a patent following reexamination will have the same effect as specified in 35 U.S.C. 252 for reissued patents regarding intervening rights for prior makers, users, purchasers, or importers (35 U.S.C. 307(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The intervening-rights situation parallels reissue; case law such as Fortel Corp. v. Phone-Mate and Kaufman Co. v. Lantech, Inc. is relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ways an ex parte reexamination may conclude
rubrics_metrics.description: Ex parte reexamination proceedings may conclude by: (A) denial, vacating, or termination of reexamination (no certificate issued); (B) issuance of a Reexamination Certificate under 37 CFR 1.570(b); (C) merged conclusion with a reissue proceeding resulting in reissue patent serving as certificate; or (D) merged conclusion with an inter partes reexamination with a single reexamination certificate issued (37 CFR references).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different administrative processing and refund implications apply depending on the mode of conclusion (see MPEP §§2287, 1455, 2690).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination of a reexamination: basis for consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: A reexamination request filed on a patent for which a reexamination certificate has already issued is considered based on the claims in the patent as modified by the previously issued reexamination certificate (not the original claims).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a 'reexamination of a reexamination' is received, the CRU prints the issued reexamination certificate and makes it of record in the new file as a preliminary amendment; examiners decide issues based on the certificate-modified claims and specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required USPTO forms for ex parte reexamination processing
rubrics_metrics.description: A specific set of USPTO forms must be used in ex parte reexamination actions and processing (e.g., PTOL-471D, PTOL-471G, PTOL-466, PTOL-467, PTOL-469, PTOL-475, PTOL-473, PTOL-474, PTOL-1516, PTOL-1517, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Request for Ex Parte Reexamination Transmittal Form (PTO/SB/57) is available but not mandatory. Proper use of the listed forms is required in processing and communications.
